causalMechanism.primaryVector: A hypothesized local bone-repair failure pathway: at the high-risk sites the injured bone shares a region of high tensile load and comparatively low blood flow, so reparative callus is exposed to repetitive tensile strain while the perfusion needed to consolidate it is limited, which is held to produce delayed union, nonunion and refracture; the located review's union-time contrast (13.1 versus 20.9 weeks) and the high non-surgical nonunion rate are consistent with a site- and loading-dependent reparative limit, but no anchor measures the mechanism directly and treatment selection confounds the modality contrast, so the route is stated as hypothesized rather than established.
causalMechanism.secondaryVector: Treatment modality, post-injury loading and return-to-activity timing are independent determinants that the located evidence measures as outcomes of the management decision rather than of the stress fracture itself, and the anchors do not separate those operational factors from intrinsic site biology.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY on one narrative review and one systematic review and deliberately not beyond them. The located evidence establishes that a high-risk stress-fracture subset carries greater risk of fracture progression, delayed healing and nonunion (femoral neck tension side, patella, anterior tibia, medial malleolus, talus, tarsal navicular, proximal fifth metatarsal, great-toe sesamoids; PMID 26972260) and quantifies adverse healing for one of those sites: 13 studies and 393 proximal-fifth-metatarsal fractures showing 87 percent union after surgical treatment versus 56 percent after non-surgical treatment, nonunion 4 versus 33 percent, delayed union 3 versus 0 percent, refracture 7 versus 12 percent, at Level IV with methodological quality assessed as low (PMID 33615403). Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual: the outcome is the same injury failing to heal rather than a second disease; the modality contrast is a treatment comparison subject to selection; the narrative review's own overall prognosis statement (stress fractures generally have an excellent prognosis with little risk of complication) bounds the claim; the anchors never measure malunion; and the batch-95 screen did not locate a third site-specific outcome anchor, so the multi-site statement rests on the narrative review alone. All references remain unverified pending qualified-human citation verification under docs/citation-verification-sop.md; this adjacency edge and the authored-corpus registration landed together on 2026-10-04 as batch 95 of the D1 draft-authoring series and carry the same conservative framing.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Anchor-tier and coverage: only two anchors were located — a narrative review supplying the multi-site high-risk framing without outcome quantification (PMID 26972260) and one systematic review whose pooled outcomes cover the proximal fifth metatarsal ONLY (PMID 33615403) — and no third site-specific outcome anchor was located in the batch-95 screen. Design limits: the systematic review is Level IV with methodological quality assessed as low, uses a simplified pooling technique across mostly small non-randomized series, and states that its non-surgical evidence is limited by underreporting (return-to-pre-injury-sport time reported for 6 non-surgically treated fractures against 117 surgical). Treatment-selection confounding: the union, nonunion and refracture figures are stratified by the treatment actually received, so the surgical-versus-non-surgical differences reflect which fractures were selected for which management and cannot be read as treatment effects or as a property of the stress fracture alone. No malunion-specific outcome: the anchors measure delayed union, nonunion and refracture; no located anchor measures malunion, so the registered evidence covers part of the umbrella target identity only. No individual-level trajectory: no anchor reports how many stress fractures progress to nonunion per individual follow-up, quantifies stress-fracture grade or site-specific exposure for any individual, or separates intrinsic site biology from re-injury, return-to-loading timing and treatment choice.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Normal healing-timeline variation: the located surgical cohort still required 13.1 weeks to radiological union and 56 percent of non-surgically treated fractures united, so a slow-healing but progressing fracture is not a nonunion
Re-injury or premature return to loading rather than a failure of intrinsic biology, which the located anchors do not separate from site factors

Treatment effects and treatment-selection: the modality contrast (87 versus 56 percent union; 4 versus 33 percent nonunion) reflects which fractures were selected for surgery, and surgical complications such as infection or hardware failure are treatment consequences rather than secondary conditions

Alternative intrinsic healing impairments documented in the individual record: vitamin D deficiency, hypogonadism, diabetes, smoking, alcohol use, thyroid disease, nutritional deficiency, and medication effects (corticosteroids, NSAIDs, fluoroquinolones)

Alternative pathology at the same site presenting as a non-healing lesion — bone cysts, bone tumors, osteomyelitis or malignancy — which are the target identity's other registered incoming windows and must be excluded by imaging and, where indicated, histology
Misclassification of the original injury (an acute or low-risk fracture misdiagnosed as a stress fracture), altering the expected healing trajectory

outgoingEdges.rationale: This adjacency edge opens the batch-95 stress-fractures to malunion-nonunion-of-fractures route as the adjacency layer's fifth authored edge, landing together with the authored-corpus registration on 2026-10-04. The located evidence establishes that a high-risk stress-fracture subset — the femoral neck tension side, patella, anterior tibia, medial malleolus, talus, tarsal navicular, proximal fifth metatarsal and great-toe sesamoids, sharing a region of high tensile load and low blood flow — carries greater risk of fracture progression, delayed healing and nonunion while stress fractures overall carry an excellent prognosis with little risk of complication (PMID 26972260), and it quantifies adverse healing for the proximal fifth metatarsal at systematic-review level: 13 studies and 393 fractures, union 87 percent (95 percent CI 83-90) after surgical versus 56 percent (41-70) after non-surgical treatment, nonunion 4 percent (2-6) versus 33 percent (20-47), delayed union 3 percent (1-5) versus 0 percent (0-8), refracture 7 percent (4-10) versus 12 percent (5-24), union time 13.1 versus 20.9 weeks, Level IV with methodological quality low and non-surgical evidence limited by underreporting (PMID 33615403). The edge is deliberately ASSOCIATION_ONLY: no located anchor establishes that a stress fracture caused an individual's malunion or nonunion; the outcome is the same injury failing to heal rather than a second disease; the per-modality contrast is a treatment comparison subject to selection; the anchors never measure malunion; and no anchor isolates intrinsic site biology from re-injury, return-to-loading timing and treatment choice. Anchor-tier discipline: only two anchors were located and the gap is disclosed on the face of the edge — the multi-site statement rests on the narrative review alone while the quantification covers one named high-risk site, and the overall prognosis statement is carried as calibration against over-reading the subset. Target-scope discipline: the target identity is the umbrella malunion-nonunion-of-fractures while the evidence measures delayed union, nonunion and refracture only, so the evidence covers part of the identity; the progression reading is disclosed (same-injury outcome, no double-counting and no chain claim). Window discipline: the target already carries draft rank-1 incoming windows from bone-cysts and bone-tumors, so this is a THIRD etiologic family (biomechanical overuse alongside structural/neoplastic pathobiology); the three windows share no PMID, are additive mechanism families rather than corroboration, and may not be pooled. This is the only registered window from stress-fractures; the batch-83 registered incoming edge sever-s-disease to stress-fractures is unaffected and no chain from sever-s-disease through stress-fractures to the malunion target is claimed; any second outgoing window from stress-fractures or a malunion-first reverse window would require npm run audit:crg redundancy adjudication before authoring. The route's anchors (PMID 26972260, PMID 33615403) were confirmed absent from the registry and cleared by source-status preflight with zero blocking flags on 2026-10-04; they enter verified:false pending qualified-human citation verification under docs/citation-verification-sop.md, and the authored-corpus suggestion, the registry lockstep (one relationship row, two source entities) and this adjacency node landed together on 2026-10-04.
